status.en: 79 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 23% fewer than the week before, most of them in Islamabad, Kabul and Peshawar.
status.nb: 79 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 23 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Islamabad, Kabul og Peshawar.

summary.en: Recent violence continues across the Pakistan-Afghanistan border area, with Afghan landmine and unexploded ordnance explosions killing dozens of civilians and a separate incident killing two people in northern Afghanistan. In Pakistan, a stone-laden truck overturned onto a loader in Ahmedpur East, killing seven, while a shooting at a funeral gathering in Sajawal Village resulted in one death, and a land-dispute-related firing in Bannu killed three. Afghan migrants near the Iran border were found shot dead, indicating cross-border insecurity. The conflict still produced 1,794 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Vold fortsetter i grenseområdet mellom Pakistan og Afghanistan, der afghanske landminer og udetonerte ammunisjonsutbrudd har drept dusinvis av sivile, og en separat hendelse har drept to personer i Nord-Afghanistan. I Pakistan veltet en steinbelastet lastebil over på en lastebil i Ahmedpur East, og syv personer ble drept, mens en skyting på en begravelsesgathering i Sajawal Village resulterte i ett dødsfall, og en skyting i forbindelse med en jordkonflikt i Bannu drepte tre. Afghanske migranter nær grensen til Iran ble funnet skutt død, noe som indikerer grenseoverskridende usikkerhet. Konflikten førte fortsatt til 1 794 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
